title: Yaw Rate / ESP Sensor Circuit (C0050)
shortDescription: Yaw rate / ESP sensor circuit fault stored as C0050.
fullDescription: The chassis controller reports a yaw or stability sensor circuit issue under C0050. Stability control disables until cleared, and a calibration is usually required after repair.
safetyImpact: Stability and traction control are disabled; lateral grip events have no electronic backup.

causes.cause: Failed yaw rate / lateral G sensor cluster
Sensor not initialized after replacement / alignment
Damaged wiring or connector at center console

fixSteps.title: Scan All Chassis Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Pull DTCs from ABS, ESP, EPS, and SAS modules; correlate which sees the fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor Mounting
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the yaw sensor is bolted tight to its bracket and the bracket is undamaged.

fixSteps.title: Check Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Test power, ground, and CAN signal at the sensor connector against schematic.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM sensor, perform steering angle and yaw zero-point calibration on level ground.

faq.q: Is the car safe to drive without ESP?
faq.a: It will drive, but stability control is disabled — be especially careful in rain or snow.

faq.q: Why after wheel alignment?
faq.a: Many vehicles require a steering angle and yaw zero relearn after alignment; skipping it sets these codes.

title: Wheel Speed Sensor Left Front Intermittent (C0210)
shortDescription: Left front wheel speed sensor circuit intermittent — C0210.
fullDescription: The ABS module reports an intermittent fault on the left front wheel speed sensor. Often caused by debris on the tone ring, a chafed harness, or a hairline-cracked sensor tip.
safetyImpact: ABS and stability control rely on this signal; loss disables anti-lock braking on this corner.

causes.cause: Chafed sensor wiring at chassis pass-through

symptoms: Intermittent ABS activation on smooth pavement

fixSteps.title: Read Live Speed Data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare all four wheel speeds while driving; the affected wheel will drop out intermittently.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor and Tone Ring
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the sensor and check for debris; rotate the wheel and inspect the tone ring teeth.

fixSteps.title: Check Bearing Play
fixSteps.instruction: Excessive radial play increases the air gap and causes intermittent dropout.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor / Hub
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM sensor; if the tone ring is part of the hub, replace the hub assembly.

faq.q: Why intermittent only?
faq.a: Heat-expansion of a cracked sensor or a slightly bent tone ring causes signal loss only under specific conditions.

faq.q: Can I drive with this?
faq.a: Yes, but ABS and stability control are degraded — drive gently, especially in wet conditions.

title: Steering Angle Sensor Position Circuit (C0710)
shortDescription: Steering angle / position sensor circuit fault stored as C0710.
fullDescription: The chassis or EPS module reports a steering angle sensor problem under C0710. ESP, ABS, lane keep, and adaptive cruise are disabled until calibration completes.
safetyImpact: ADAS and stability systems lose a key reference, disabling lane keep, ESP, and adaptive cruise.

causes.cause: Steering angle sensor not calibrated after alignment
Damaged ribbon cable in steering column
Worn steering coupler creating angle error

fixSteps.title: Calibrate SAS
fixSteps.instruction: With wheels straight, perform OEM steering angle zero-point calibration.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Clockspring
fixSteps.instruction: Check for binding or audible cable damage; many platforms integrate SAS into the clockspring.

fixSteps.title: Verify CAN Bus
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm SAS is communicating on the chassis CAN with no missing-message faults.

fixSteps.title: Replace Assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the SAS or clockspring assembly with OEM and recalibrate.

faq.q: Can I calibrate SAS myself?
faq.a: Many vehicles support a self-learn after a straight drive; others require a scan tool routine.

faq.q: Why does this also light the airbag?
faq.a: On vehicles where SAS is built into the clockspring, a clockspring failure trips both circuits.

title: Air Suspension Level Height Sensor (C1500)
shortDescription: Air suspension ride height sensor fault stored as C1500.
fullDescription: The air suspension module sees an out-of-range or implausible height sensor signal under C1500. Auto-leveling is disabled and the corner may not raise.
safetyImpact: Loss of ride height control affects headlight aim and handling, especially when loaded.

causes.cause: Wiring chafe at suspension travel point

fixSteps.title: Read Ride Height Live Data
fixSteps.instruction: Measure each corner with a tape and compare to PID values from the suspension module.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Linkage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the height sensor link is intact and not bent from off-road or curb contact.

fixSteps.title: Check for Air Leaks
fixSteps.instruction: Use soapy water on bags, lines, and valve block while the system is pressurized.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM sensor, perform ride height calibration to spec.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive low?
faq.a: Briefly, yes, but tires and inner fenders can rub. Avoid speed bumps and load.

faq.q: Should I add a leveling kit instead?
faq.a: Bypassing air suspension creates new ride and DTC issues; repair is usually preferable.

fixSteps.instruction: Use soapy water on bags, lines, and valve block while the system is pressurized.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM sensor, perform ride height calibration to spec.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive low?
faq.a: Briefly, yes, but tires and inner fenders can rub. Avoid speed bumps and load.

faq.q: Should I add a leveling kit instead?
faq.a: Bypassing air suspension creates new ride and DTC issues; repair is usually preferable.

title: Lateral Acceleration Sensor Sensor Circuit (C1800)
shortDescription: Lateral acceleration sensor circuit fault stored as C1800.
fullDescription: The stability control module reports the lateral G sensor signal out of range under C1800. ESP, roll stability, and trailer sway control disable until cleared.
safetyImpact: Stability and trailer-sway systems are disabled, which can be critical when towing or in crosswinds.

causes.cause: CAN message dropout from sensor cluster

fixSteps.title: Verify Sensor Output
fixSteps.instruction: Read live data while gently rocking the vehicle; output should change with body motion.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Mounting
fixSteps.instruction: Check the bracket and bolts; any movement creates intermittent faults.

fixSteps.title: Check CAN
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm no missing-message DTCs from ESP module pointing back to this sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM sensor, perform vehicle stationary calibration.

faq.q: Why did this code appear after a tire change?
faq.a: If the vehicle was on a hoist with wheels hanging, an over-range fault can latch and need clearing.

faq.q: Are these sensors directional?
faq.a: Yes — most are keyed and labeled. Installing rotated sets immediate codes.

title: Yaw Rate / ESP System Variant Not Programmed (C0561)
shortDescription: ESP system variant not programmed / configuration mismatch — C0561.
fullDescription: A generic GM-family stability control DTC indicating the ESP/ABS module configuration does not match the vehicle. Common after module replacement without VIN/option coding.
safetyImpact: Stability and traction control are disabled; lateral grip events have no electronic backup.

causes.cause: Failed yaw rate / lateral G sensor cluster
Sensor not initialized after replacement / alignment
Damaged wiring or connector at center console

fixSteps.title: Scan All Chassis Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Pull DTCs from ABS, ESP, EPS, and SAS modules; correlate which sees the fault.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor Mounting
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the yaw sensor is bolted tight to its bracket and the bracket is undamaged.

fixSteps.title: Check Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Test power, ground, and CAN signal at the sensor connector against schematic.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Install OEM sensor, perform steering angle and yaw zero-point calibration on level ground.

faq.q: Is the car safe to drive without ESP?
faq.a: It will drive, but stability control is disabled — be especially careful in rain or snow.

faq.q: Why after wheel alignment?
faq.a: Many vehicles require a steering angle and yaw zero relearn after alignment; skipping it sets these codes.
